boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented landmarks along Oneonta’s historic Main Street corridor, an easy walk from SUNY Oneonta’s campus-adjacent downtown.

cards.title: See local history at 183 Main
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 183 Main Street
cards.notes: Start at the museum’s historic brick building, then use its exhibits and resource library to orient yourself to Oneonta’s local history.
cards.short_summary: A history museum and archive in Main Street’s oldest brick building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greater Oneonta Historical Society houses arts, artifacts, archives, exhibitions, a resource library, and a gift shop at 183 Main Street; admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit the Oneonta History Center & Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum lists summer hours of Tuesday–Friday 12–4 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; check its site before visiting.

cards.title: Spot the Oneonta Hotel details
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 189–201 Main Street
cards.notes: Pause across from Muller Plaza to look up at the Beaux Arts facade, especially its lion heads and Ionic columns.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic Main Street hotel building with distinctive exterior details.
cards.evidence_claim: The historical society’s walking tour identifies the Oneonta Hotel at 189–201 Main Street and describes its lion heads, Ionic columns, and Beaux Arts building.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from the Main Street public corridor.

cards.entity_name: Historic F. W. Woolworth and J. J. Newberry buildings
cards.title: Trace Main Street’s chain-store past
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 203–205 and 221–223 Main Street
cards.notes: Use the tour’s paired stops to compare these storefront blocks and learn how national chains once occupied Main Street.
cards.short_summary: Two Main Street addresses documented as former Woolworth’s and Newberry’s locations.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies the historic F. W. Woolworth and J. J. Newberry buildings at 203–205 and 221–223 Main Street.
cards.access_notes: View the addressed building exteriors along Main Street.

cards.title: Find the bank’s phased facade
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 233–241 Main Street
cards.notes: Walk past this block and look for the building’s different construction phases, beginning with its west wing in 1907.
cards.short_summary: A former bank building whose construction began with a west wing in 1907.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies Historic Wilber National Bank at 233–241 Main Street and states that its building was constructed in four phases beginning in 1907.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from Main Street.

cards.title: Read the former City Hall facade
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 242 Main Street
cards.notes: Stop at the former city hall to examine its Neo-Classical Revival and Beaux Arts design from the Main Street sidewalk.
cards.short_summary: Oneonta’s first city hall, built in 1906.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies the Municipal Building at 242 Main Street as Oneonta’s first city hall, built in 1906 in Neo-Classical Revival and Beaux Arts styles.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from Main Street.

cards.title: Find the saved Old Post Office
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 258 Main Street
cards.notes: Look at the current City Hall and read its reuse story: community opposition prevented the former post office’s demolition.
cards.short_summary: A former post office adaptively reused as Oneonta City Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies the Old Post Office/City Hall at 258 Main Street and says it was saved from demolition and adaptively reused as Oneonta’s City Hall.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from Main Street; City Hall access depends on municipal operations.

cards.title: Pause at Riverside Cemetery
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 296 Main Street
cards.notes: Approach respectfully behind First Presbyterian Church and use the tour context to understand why this is Oneonta’s most historic cemetery.
cards.short_summary: A historic cemetery behind First Presbyterian Church.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies Riverside Cemetery at 296 Main Street as Oneonta’s most historic cemetery and dates the land deed for church, parsonage, and cemetery to 1805.
cards.access_notes: Use respectful cemetery etiquette and follow any posted access guidance.

cards.title: Look for the Fairchild Mansion’s style
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 322 Main Street
cards.notes: View this landmark from the sidewalk and compare its Italianate origins with the Queen Anne remodeling documented on the walking tour.
cards.short_summary: An 1867 mansion later remodeled in the Queen Anne style.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies Fairchild Mansion/Masonic Lodge at 322 Main Street, built in 1867 and remodeled in 1891 in the Queen Anne style.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from Main Street; do not assume public interior access.

cards.title: See the saved Ford Block
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 192–202 Main Street
cards.notes: Walk this block and use the tour’s account of the 1881 fire and later preservation to add context to the streetscape.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street commercial block saved after a proposed urban-renewal demolition.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour identifies Ford Block at 192–202 Main Street and states that it was built after an 1881 fire and later saved from planned demolition.
cards.access_notes: View the block from the Main Street public corridor.

cards.title: Locate the Clinton-Sullivan monument
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — Clinton Plaza
cards.notes: Use the remaining strip of Brown Park at Clinton Plaza to find the monument to the 1779 Clinton-Sullivan expedition.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street plaza retaining a small remnant of Brown Park and its monument.
cards.evidence_claim: The walking tour states that Clinton Plaza retains a strip of the former Brown Park around a monument to the 1779 Clinton-Sullivan expedition.
cards.access_notes: Use public walkways and observe any posted plaza guidance.
